$comment: There is no TypeScript in this package and there is not going to be: it ships
as the .mjs files you see, with no build step, which is what makes installing it
from a git tag and running it from a fresh clone work with nothing installed.
This file exists so `npm run typecheck` can read the JSDoc that is already there
and tell us when an annotation has drifted from the code. It found two on the day
it was added: a parameter documented as a number that is a map, and a config type
missing three of its sections. Both were wrong in the types consumers import.
noImplicitAny stays off on purpose. The rules pass around plain objects parsed
from JSON and Markdown; turning it on produces a hundred annotations that make
the callbacks noisier without making one of them safer.
